title: Separate model conformance results from engineering judgments
statement: The system shall distinguish mechanically established model-conformance results from supplied engineering-review judgments when presenting an assessment, identify each subject, scope, and basis, and prevent a structural result from being presented as requirement approval, design adequacy, or requirement satisfaction.

what.problem: A passing schema or relationship check can be mistaken for evidence that the model is meaningful, complete, or implemented correctly.
what.desired_outcome: Participants understand what a result establishes and which conclusions still require engineering assessment.

why.rationale: IR-005 assigns clarity, derivation, allocation adequacy, assumptions, and evidence adequacy to engineering review rather than mechanical conformance.

conditions: When presenting a model-conformance result alone or alongside a supplied engineering-review judgment.

contexts: Within assessment of the selected engineering model and its declared rules.

how.approach: Label the kind, subjects, governing rules, and assessed scope of each result. Keep supplied engineering judgments attributable to their review basis and separate from mechanical findings. Expose a review need where the rules cannot decide adequacy, without manufacturing a positive or negative judgment.

how_much.scope: Covers presentation and interpretation of model-assessment outcomes, including supplied judgments; it does not create or approve those judgments. Review authority and controlled adoption belong to IR-003; evidence-backed satisfaction and its applicability belong to IR-004. This obligation constrains existing assessment behavior without introducing a separate Function merely to mirror this SR.

acceptance_criteria: A successful mechanical result states which rules and state were checked and does not report the requirement approved, implemented, or satisfied.
Present two structurally valid definitions with different clarity or unsupported reasoning; leave adequacy to identified engineering review rather than inferring it from structural success.

When a supplied review judgment accompanies a mechanical result, preserve its identified subject and basis and present it distinctly from the mechanical observation; do not infer or fabricate review approval.
An allocation result needing semantic review is not silently promoted to a mechanically established conflict or a confirmed adequate design.

sources.basis: Derived from IR-005 and its selected initial-profile scope: IR-005 assigns clarity, derivation, allocation adequacy, assumptions, and evidence adequacy to engineering review rather than mechanical conformance.
